findings.problem: The blank is the next words of the same line in Isaiah 55:1 ("without money and without cost"). Card 1 quoted the first half of the verse, and this card asks the baker to fill in the rest of the wording. "Cost" adds no meaning beyond "without money", so the card tests the verse's wording, not something the baker can reason out. This is a prophetic passage.

rule.text: In poetry, letters and prophecy, the rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Stop 2 card 1 says "the voice shifts" (Isaiah 55:6-7 speaks of the LORD in the third person). Card 4 then quotes a first-person line ("For My thoughts are not your thoughts...") and only names the speaker at the end, through the BSB's "declares the LORD". Right after a voice shift, the baker reads "My" without knowing who is speaking. The card should say the LORD is speaking before the quote starts.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The question opens "In this joyful picture", which points back to story cards the baker can no longer see. Calling it "joyful" also gives the answer away, because thornbushes and briers spreading is plainly not joyful, so the setup rules out the wrong answer.

rule.text: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
